title: DOE announces grants for SiC cladding research and testing
summary: On October 5, the Department of Energy announced that it plans to award up to $50 million in grants over three years to support research on the use of silicon carbide (SiC) as fuel cladding material. The DOE touts SiC for what it says is the material’s potential to improve the safety and cost efficiency of light water reactors currently operating in the United States and said that research into SiC cladding could further the development of fuels for forthcoming reactors.

title: Rising together: Collaborative project delivery for the nuclear fleet
summary: Karen Fili As the nuclear industry enters one of the most significant investment periods in its history, utilities are managing unprecedented capital portfolios while simultaneously preparing for long-term operation, plant modernization, extended power uprates, digital transformation, workforce challenges, and new nuclear opportunities. No single utility can solve these challenges alone. For the past 30 years, Utilities Service Alliance (USA) has demonstrated that collaboration across utilities creates measurable value. What began as an organization focused on sharing operational excellence has evolved into an alliance that supports nearly every aspect of nuclear performance—from safety culture and operational excellence to maintenance, engineering, equipment reliability, supply chain, and now, to large-scale capital project execution.

title: Supplier Showcase focus: AI-driven diagnostics
summary: The American Nuclear Society is hosting a Supplier Showcase webinar, “From Alarm to Answer: How AI Can Reduce Equipment Load and Enhance Performance,” on October 13, from 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. (CDT) in partnership with Nuclearn, a provider of AI tools purpose-built for the nuclear industry.

title: Entergy’s Louisiana utilities monitoring Tropical Storm Isaias
summary: Entergy Louisiana and Entergy New Orleans are closely monitoring Tropical Storm Isaias in the Gulf and are preparing for severe weather that could impact our service territory within the next several days.
